howTo: Sit at a low cable and hold one handle with your arm straight.
Row your elbow back toward your hip.
Reach forward and let your shoulder go forward at the end.
exercises.tip: Don't twist your torso to move the weight.

howto.setup: Sit or stand facing a mid pulley holding one handle.
cues: Row the elbow back past your torso
howto.mistake: Twisting the torso to pull.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
exercises.description: A seated cable row with a wide overhand grip pulled to the upper chest, for the upper back and rear delts.
howTo: Sit at a low cable holding a wide bar overhand.
Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows flared to about 60 degrees.
Return slowly until your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Stay tall. Don't rock back to finish the rep.

howto.setup: Sit at the cable row with a wide bar and an overhand grip.
cues: Pull the bar to your upper stomach
Drive the elbows out and back
howto.mistake: Rocking far back to move the stack.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A Romanian deadlift with dumbbells, for the hamstrings and glutes at long length.
howTo: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with soft knees.
Push your hips back, sliding the weights down your legs, until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.tip: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs the whole way.

howto.setup: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs, knees soft.
cues: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs
howto.mistake: Rounding the back to reach the floor.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: A squat holding one dumbbell at your chest, an easy way to learn deep, upright squatting.
howTo: Hold a dumbbell upright at your chest with both hands.
Sit down between your hips, keeping your elbows inside your knees.
Go deep, then drive back up.
exercises.tip: Use your elbows to nudge your knees out at the bottom.

howto.setup: Hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest with elbows tucked.
howto.mistake: Letting the dumbbell pull your torso forward.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: A reverse lunge with dumbbells, gentler on the knees than a forward lunge.
howTo: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front foot to return, then switch legs.
exercises.tip: A longer step works the glutes more; a shorter one works the quads more.

howto.setup: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides.
cues: Lower the back knee toward the floor
Drive through the front foot to stand
howto.mistake: Leaning forward and pushing off the back foot.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: A seated dumbbell press that starts palms in and rotates outward as you press.
howTo: Sit holding dumbbells at chin height with your palms facing you.
Press up, rotating your palms to face forward as you go.
Reverse the rotation as you lower.
exercises.tip: Keep the rotation smooth. It's part of the press, not a separate move.

howto.setup: Sit with dumbbells at chin height, palms facing you.
cues: Rotate palms forward as you press
Reverse the rotation on the way down
howto.mistake: Rushing the rotation and losing control.

exercises.name: Cable Y-Raise
exercises.description: A raise from crossed low cables up into a Y shape, for the side delts and lower traps.
howTo: Stand between two low pulleys and cross the cables so each hand holds the opposite handle.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y above shoulder height.
Lower slowly back across your body.
exercises.tip: Use light weight. Your shoulders should do this, not your back.

howto.setup: Stand between two low pulleys holding the opposite handles.
cues: Raise the arms up in a Y shape
howto.mistake: Shrugging the traps up as the arms rise.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.description: A seated one-arm curl with your elbow braced on your inner thigh, for strict biceps work.
howTo: Sit with your elbow against the inside of your thigh, dumbbell hanging.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulder.
Lower until your arm is straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your upper arm completely still.

howto.setup: Sit with your elbow braced against your inner thigh, holding a dumbbell.
cues: Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder
howto.mistake: Swinging the torso to lift the weight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.description: A bent-over triceps extension with a dumbbell, hardest at the fully straightened position.
howTo: Hinge forward with your upper arm pinned at your side, elbow bent.
Straighten your arm back until it's fully locked.
Lower slowly to 90 degrees.
exercises.tip: Raise the elbow a little higher than your torso to keep tension on.

howto.setup: Hinge forward with your upper arm parallel to your torso.
howto.mistake: Swinging the upper arm.

exercises.name: JM Press
exercises.description: A hybrid of a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher that lets you load the triceps heavy.
howTo: Lie on a bench holding the bar with a close grip over your chest.
Lower by bending your elbows and letting the bar travel toward your upper chest or chin.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Start light. The hybrid path takes a few sessions to learn.

howto.setup: Lie on a bench with a close grip on the bar over your chest.
cues: Lower the bar toward your chin by bending elbows forward
howto.mistake: Letting it turn into a regular bench press.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat
exercises.description: A knee-dominant squat where you lean back as your knees go forward, stretching the quads including the rectus femoris.
howTo: Hold a support with one hand and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Lean back as you bend your knees forward and down, keeping your hips straight.
Go as low as you can control, then push back up.
exercises.tip: Keep a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.

howto.setup: Stand in a sissy squat station or hold a support with heels anchored.
cues: Lean back as the knees move forward
Rise back up with the quads
howto.mistake: Bending at the hips into a regular squat.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row under a fixed bar or rings, which you can make harder by lowering the bar or raising your feet.
howTo: Lie under a bar set at about waist height and grip it with your arms straight.
Keep your body straight and pull your chest to the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.

howto.setup: Hang under a bar set at waist height with body straight and heels on the floor.
cues: Pull your chest to the bar
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hips raised high so you press at an overhead angle, a bodyweight shoulder press.
howTo: Start in a push-up position and walk your feet in until your hips are high.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Raise your feet on a box to make it harder.

howto.setup: Set up in a push-up position, then walk your feet in so your hips are high.
cues: Lower your head toward the floor in front of your hands
howto.mistake: Dropping the hips into a regular push-up.

exercises.name: Weighted Decline Crunch
exercises.description: A crunch on a decline bench holding a plate, for loaded ab work.
howTo: Hook your feet on the decline bench and hold a plate at your chest.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis to lift your upper back.
Lower slowly until your abs stretch.
exercises.tip: Curl up. Don't swing up by pulling with the hips.

howto.setup: Hook your feet on a decline bench and hold a plate at your chest.
cues: Curl the torso up one vertebra at a time
howto.mistake: Pulling up with the hip flexors instead of curling.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.description: A standing diagonal cable chop for the obliques.
howTo: Set a cable high, stand side-on and grab the handle with both hands.
Pull it down and across your body to the opposite hip, rotating through your torso.
Return slowly along the same diagonal.
exercises.tip: Pivot your back foot so your hips can turn with you.

howto.setup: Stand side-on to a high pulley holding the handle with both hands.
cues: Rotate down and across your body
howto.mistake: Pulling with the arms instead of rotating.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.description: An anti-rotation press: you hold a cable straight out in front while it tries to twist you.
howTo: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle at your chest.
Press it straight out until your arms are straight, without letting your torso turn.
Hold briefly, then bring it back.
exercises.tip: Brace like someone is about to push you sideways.

howto.setup: Stand side-on to a chest-height pulley holding the handle at your chest.
howto.mistake: Letting the torso twist toward the stack.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Crunch
exercises.description: A standing rope crunch, a quick loaded ab exercise when the kneeling version isn't comfortable.
howTo: Face away from a high cable, holding the rope by your head.
Crunch down by curling your ribs toward your hips.
Return slowly until your abs stretch.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips still. Only your spine curls.

howto.setup: Face away from a high pulley holding the rope beside your head.
cues: Crunch your ribs toward your hips
howto.mistake: Bending at the hips instead of curling the spine.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
exercises.description: A chest-down Y-raise on an incline bench for the lower traps and rear delts.
howTo: Lie face down on a bench at 30 to 45 degrees holding light dumbbells.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y with your thumbs up.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Very light weight. Squeeze the shoulder blades down and back.

howto.setup: Lie face down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging.
cues: Raise the arms in a Y shape
howto.mistake: Using heavy dumbbells and swinging.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: A crossed-cable reverse fly that keeps tension on the rear delts through the full arc.
howTo: Set both pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables, holding the opposite handle in each hand.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc.
Return slowly until your hands cross.
exercises.tip: Pull wide, not back. Think of moving your hands apart.

howto.setup: Stand between two pulleys at shoulder height holding opposite cables.
cues: Sweep the arms back and out
howto.mistake: Pinching the shoulder blades hard to pull with the back.

exercises.name: Overhead Rope Triceps Extension (Low Cable)
exercises.description: An overhead rope extension from a low pulley, facing away, which stretches the long head under load.
howTo: Hold a rope behind your head with your back to a low cable.
Extend your arms overhead until they are straight.
Lower slowly until your elbows are fully bent.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows close to your head.

howto.setup: Face away from a low pulley holding a rope behind your head.
howto.mistake: Letting the elbows drift apart.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.description: A standing kickback from a low cable with an ankle strap, isolating one glute.
howTo: Attach an ankle strap and face the stack, holding on for support.
Kick your leg back by squeezing your glute.
Return slowly.
exercises.tip: Lean forward a little so you get a longer range.

howto.setup: Hinge forward holding a low pulley handle with the upper arm by your torso.
howto.mistake: Swinging the arm to finish reps.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: A dumbbell fly on an incline bench, for the upper chest at long length.
howTo: Lie on a bench set at 30 degrees holding dumbbells over your chest, palms facing.
With a slight elbow bend, open your arms wide until your chest stretches.
Bring them back together over your chest.
exercises.tip: Stop the stretch where your shoulders still feel good.

howto.setup: Lie on a 30-degree incline holding dumbbells over your upper chest.
cues: Bring the bells together over your chest
howto.mistake: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows.

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A barbell bench press on a decline, biasing the lower chest with less front-delt work.
howTo: Hook your legs under the pads on a decline bench and unrack the bar with a medium grip.
Lower it to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Always use a spotter or safeties. Unracking at a decline is awkward.

howto.setup: Hook your legs on a decline bench and unrack the bar over your chest.
howto.mistake: Bouncing off the chest.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.description: A curl with an angled EZ bar, which is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
howTo: Stand holding the EZ bar on the angled grips, arms straight.
Curl it up, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Lower to straight arms.
exercises.tip: No swinging. Let the biceps do the lifting.

howto.setup: Hold an EZ bar on the angled grips in front of your thighs.
howto.mistake: Leaning back to swing the bar.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.description: A curl lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, which loads the biceps hardest at the top.
howTo: Lie face down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging straight down.
Curl up without letting your elbows move forward.
Lower to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Squeeze hard at the top. That's where this one is hardest.

howto.setup: Lie face down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight down.
howto.mistake: Moving the upper arms forward.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Reverse Curl
exercises.description: An overhand-grip curl for the brachioradialis and forearm extensors.
howTo: Hold an EZ bar overhand at shoulder width, arms straight.
Curl it up, keeping your wrists straight.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Use less weight than a regular curl and keep the wrists neutral.

howto.setup: Hold an EZ bar or barbell with an overhand grip.
howto.mistake: Letting the wrists bend back.

exercises.name: Cable Preacher Curl
exercises.description: A preacher curl with a cable, so the biceps stay loaded at the stretched bottom.
howTo: Set a preacher bench in front of a low cable and take a bar or handle.
Curl up until your forearms are nearly vertical.
Lower to almost straight.
exercises.tip: Control the bottom, where the stretch is.

howto.setup: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley.
cues: Curl up without lifting the elbows
howto.mistake: Lifting the elbows off the pad.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Curl
exercises.description: A one-leg machine leg curl done standing, for each hamstring on its own.
howTo: Stand in the machine with the pad just above your heel.
Curl your heel toward your glute.
Lower slowly to straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips pressed into the pad.

howto.setup: Stand at the machine with the pad behind your ankle.
cues: Curl the heel toward your glute
howto.mistake: Swinging the hip to start the curl.

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise
exercises.description: A hamstring exercise on a glute-ham bench that trains knee flexion and hip extension together.
howTo: Set your feet against the plate with your knees just behind the pad.
Lower your torso forward under control until your body is horizontal.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings.
exercises.tip: Push your toes into the plate to help start the pull.

howto.setup: Set your feet on the plate with knees just behind the pad.
cues: Curl back up with the hamstrings
howto.mistake: Bending at the hips to make it easier.

exercises.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A hip thrust done with your back on the floor, with a shorter range but quick to set up.
howTo: Lie on the floor with a padded bar across your hips and your knees bent.
Drive through your heels to raise your hips until they're in line with your body.
Squeeze, then lower.
exercises.tip: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down.

howto.setup: Lie on the floor with the padded bar over your hips and knees bent.
cues: Squeeze the glutes at the top
howto.mistake: Pushing through the toes.

exercises.name: Good Morning
exercises.description: A barbell hinge with the bar on your back, for the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and stand with soft knees.
Push your hips back and lower your chest until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
exercises.tip: Start light. The long lever loads the lower back quickly.

howto.setup: Set the bar on your upper back with feet hip width and knees soft.
cues: Stand by driving the hips forward
howto.mistake: Rounding the back to go deeper.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A lateral raise done seated, so you can't cheat the weight up with your legs.
howTo: Sit on the end of a bench holding dumbbells at your sides.
Raise them out to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Stop at shoulder height and keep your shoulders down.

howto.setup: Sit on a bench with dumbbells at your sides.
cues: Raise the arms to shoulder height
howto.mistake: Leaning to swing the weight up.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands on plates or handles so your chest can go below hand level for a deeper stretch.
howTo: Set two plates or handles shoulder-width apart and get into a push-up position.
Lower until your chest is below your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.

howto.setup: Set your hands on plates or handles so your chest can sink below hand level.
cues: Lower until your chest passes your hands
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag.

exercises.name: Seated Row Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A selectorized seated row with a chest pad and fixed handles, which keeps the torso still so the mid-back and lats do the work.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles are at about lower-chest height, with your chest on the pad.
Row the handles back until your elbows pass your torso.
Let them go forward until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the pad. Don't lean back to finish the rep.

howto.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest.
cues: Keep the chest on the pad
howto.mistake: Leaning back off the pad.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Row Machine
exercises.description: A plate-loaded row on a diagonal from above your head down to your waist, sitting between the High Row and a seated row and biased toward the lats.
howTo: Sit with your chest on the pad and reach up and forward for the handles.
Pull down and back on the diagonal until your elbows reach your hips.
Return slowly until your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Drive your elbows toward your back pockets.

howto.setup: Set the seat so the handles are above and ahead of you.
cues: Drive the elbows toward your hips
howto.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders as you pull.

exercises.name: Converging Arc Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A plate-loaded pulldown whose arms travel in a converging arc, matching the line of the lat fibres and loading the lats hard at the top stretch.
howTo: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up for the handles, letting your shoulders rise.
Pull down and in until your elbows are at your sides.
Return slowly all the way to the top stretch.
exercises.tip: The heaviest part is near the top. Don't cut the stretch short.

howto.setup: Sit with thighs under the pad and grip the handles overhead.
cues: Pull the handles in an arc toward your hips
howto.mistake: Rocking the torso to start the rep.

exercises.name: Standing Lateral Raise Machine
exercises.description: A standing machine lateral raise with handles, which feels like a dumbbell raise on a fixed path with more even tension.
howTo: Stand side-on or facing the machine with the pivot lined up with your shoulders, and take the handles.
Raise your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly until the stack nearly touches down.
exercises.tip: Gripping handles lets the traps help more than elbow pads do, so keep your shoulders down.

howto.setup: Stand facing the machine with pads on the outside of your arms.
cues: Raise the arms out to the sides
howto.mistake: Shrugging up to lift the pads.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Bench Press
exercises.description: A Smith bench press on a machine whose rails angle inward, so the bar travels up and slightly toward your face like a free bench, with a bit more chest focus.
howTo: Lie on the bench so the bar lines up with your mid-chest at the bottom.
Unrack, then lower under control to your chest.
Press up along the angled path to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Set the safeties just above your chest before you start.

howto.setup: Lie on the bench so the handles start over your mid-chest.
cues: Press up and in along the arc
howto.mistake: Cutting the bottom range short.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Incline Press
exercises.description: An incline Smith press on angled rails that move the bar up and back over the shoulders, for the upper chest.
howTo: Set an incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees so the bar meets your upper chest.
Lower under control to your upper chest.
Press up along the angled path.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulder blades back and your chest high.

howto.setup: Set the incline so the handles start over your upper chest.
cues: Keep your back on the pad
howto.mistake: Lifting the shoulders off the pad at lockout.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A seated overhead press on angled Smith rails that carry the bar slightly back over your head, a natural pressing path with no balance demand.
howTo: Sit on an upright bench with the bar at about chin height.
Press up along the path until your arms are straight.
Lower back to chin height.
exercises.tip: Keep your back on the pad. Don't arch to finish the rep.

howto.setup: Sit with your back on the pad and the handles at shoulder height.
howto.mistake: Arching the back off the pad.

exercises.name: Pulldown Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A selectorized lever pulldown with fixed handles, with a smoother, more stable path than a cable bar.
howTo: Sit with your thighs under the pad and take the handles.
Pull down until your elbows are at your sides.
Return slowly to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest up and pull with your elbows.

howto.setup: Adjust the thigh pad and grip the handles overhead.
cues: Pull the handles to your upper chest
howto.mistake: Leaning way back.

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Chest-Supported Row
exercises.description: A plate-loaded chest-supported row with a long lever, which loads hardest near full contraction and suits heavy upper-back work.
howTo: Set the chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms.
Row the handles back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Pause at the top for a second. The lever makes that position hardest.

howto.setup: Set your chest on the pad and grip the handles at full stretch.
cues: Keep your chest on the pad
howto.mistake: Lifting off the pad to jerk the weight.

exercises.name: Rotary Torso Machine
exercises.description: A seated machine that rotates your torso against resistance, for direct oblique work.
howTo: Sit with your knees locked in and your chest against the pads.
Rotate your torso to one side through a comfortable range.
Return slowly, then do the other side.
exercises.tip: Move slowly. Don't let the weight swing you back.

howto.setup: Sit with your knees locked under the pads and chest against the pad.
cues: Rotate the torso to one side
howto.mistake: Using momentum to swing the pad.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.description: A standing cable adduction with an ankle strap, which trains each adductor on its own and lets you go through a long range.
howTo: Attach the strap to your inside ankle and stand side-on to a low cable.
Sweep the leg across in front of the other one.
Return slowly as far as is comfortable.
exercises.tip: Stand tall and hold on. Don't lean into it.

howto.setup: Attach an ankle cuff to the near leg and stand side-on to a low pulley.
cues: Pull the leg across in front of the other
howto.mistake: Leaning the torso to help the leg across.

exercises.name: Horizontal Leg Press
exercises.description: A seated selectorized leg press that pushes straight out. It's usually lighter and easier on the lower back than a 45-degree sled, but you can't go quite as deep.
howTo: Sit with your back flat on the pad and your feet shoulder width on the platform.
Bend your knees toward your chest as far as your hips allow.
Press out until your legs are almost straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips down on the seat at the bottom.

howto.setup: Sit with your back on the pad and feet shoulder width on the plate.
cues: Lower until knees are deeply bent
howto.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward.

exercises.name: Reverse Hack Squat
exercises.description: A hack squat done facing the pad with your hips pushed back. It shifts the work from the quads toward the glutes and hamstrings.
howTo: Face the machine with your chest on the back pad and your shoulders under the pads.
Push your hips back and squat down until your hips are deeply flexed.
Drive back up through your heels.
exercises.tip: Let your hips travel back, not just down.

howto.setup: Face the pad with your chest on it and shoulders under the pads.
cues: Push the hips back as you lower
howto.mistake: Letting the heels lift.

exercises.name: Kneeling Leg Curl
exercises.description: A one-leg curl kneeling on a pad with your hip slightly bent, partway between a lying and a seated curl.
howTo: Kneel on the pad with the roller just above one heel and your forearms on the support.
Curl your heel toward your glute.
Lower slowly to straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips square on the pad.

howto.setup: Kneel on the machine with the pad behind your lower calf.
cues: Curl the heel toward your glute
howto.mistake: Lifting the hip to get more range.

exercises.name: Smith Squat (Feet Forward)
exercises.description: A Smith squat with your feet set ahead of the bar, so you can sit back and down. Compared with the standard Smith squat, it moves some of the work to the glutes.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and put your feet about a foot in front of it.
Sit down and slightly back until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up through your whole foot.
exercises.tip: Wider and further forward means more glutes. Narrower and under the bar means more quads.

howto.setup: Set your feet well in front of the Smith bar, bar on your upper back.
howto.mistake: Going so shallow the quads barely bend.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A two-dumbbell row lying face down on an incline bench, needing no machine and putting no load on the lower back.
howTo: Lie chest-down on a bench at about 30 degrees with dumbbells hanging.
Row both dumbbells up until your elbows pass your torso.
Lower to a full reach.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the bench. Don't lift it to cheat.

howto.setup: Lie chest down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging.
cues: Row the dumbbells toward your hips
Keep the chest on the pad
howto.mistake: Lifting the head and chest off the bench.

exercises.name: Seal Row
exercises.description: A barbell row lying face down on a high flat bench, so the row is strict and your lower back is completely out of it.
howTo: Lie face down on a high bench with the barbell underneath and your arms straight.
Row the bar up to the underside of the bench.
Lower to a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Use a cambered bar or blocks if the bench is too low for a full range.

howto.setup: Lie face down on a high flat bench with the bar hanging below.
cues: Pull the bar to the bench
Keep the chest on the pad
howto.mistake: Kicking the legs to jerk the bar up.

exercises.name: Yates Row
exercises.description: An underhand barbell row with your torso about 30 degrees forward of upright, which lets you row heavy and brings in more lats and biceps.
howTo: Hold the bar underhand at shoulder width and hinge to about 30 degrees.
Row it to your lower stomach, driving your elbows back.
Lower under control to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep the torso angle fixed. Don't stand up into each rep.

howto.setup: Stand holding a bar with an underhand grip and a slight forward lean.
cues: Pull the bar to your lower stomach
howto.mistake: Standing nearly upright so it turns into a shrug.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.description: A deadlift from pins at about knee height that trains heavy lockouts for the back, traps and glutes.
howTo: Set the bar on pins just below or at your knees and grip it just outside your legs.
Brace, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Lower back to the pins under control.
exercises.tip: Don't lean back at the top. Stand tall and stop.

howto.setup: Set the bar in a rack at about knee height and grip it outside your legs.
cues: Brace and pull the slack out
Drive the hips forward to lockout
howto.mistake: Leaning back hard at lockout.

exercises.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift inside a hexagonal bar with neutral handles, which keeps you more upright and shares the work between the quads and hips.
howTo: Stand in the centre of the bar and grip the handles.
Sit your hips down until your shoulders are over the handles, then brace.
Drive the floor away and stand tall.
Lower by pushing your hips back.
exercises.tip: Use the high handles to start if your mobility is limited.

howto.setup: Stand inside the trap bar with feet hip width and grip the handles.
cues: Brace and push through the floor
Stand up with hips and knees together
howto.mistake: Letting the hips rise before the bar moves.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
exercises.description: A knee raise with your forearms on a captain's chair, an easier step toward the hanging leg raise.
howTo: Support yourself on the chair's forearm pads with your back against the pad.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower slowly to straight legs.
exercises.tip: Curling the pelvis is what works the abs. Just lifting the knees mostly works the hip flexors.

howto.setup: Set your forearms on the pads and back against the back pad.
cues: Raise the knees toward your chest
howto.mistake: Swinging the legs with momentum.

exercises.name: Back Extension Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A seated selectorized back extension that trains the lower back directly with very little load on the hips.
howTo: Sit with the pad across your upper back and your feet braced.
Extend your spine back against the pad.
Return slowly forward.
exercises.tip: Move through a comfortable range. Don't snap into extension.

howto.setup: Sit with the pad across your upper back and feet set.
howto.mistake: Overarching past upright.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description: A palms-down wrist curl for the forearm extensors, the opposite side from a normal wrist curl.
howTo: Rest your forearms on a bench with your palms facing down and dumbbells in your hands.
Raise the backs of your hands toward you.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Light weight and full range. The extensors are small muscles.

howto.setup: Rest forearms on a bench, palms down, holding a bar.
howto.mistake: Using a weight so heavy the forearms lift.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.description: A heavy carry with a dumbbell or handle in each hand, for grip, upper traps and trunk stiffness.
howTo: Deadlift a heavy dumbbell or handle in each hand and stand tall.
Walk with short, quick steps for a set distance or time.
Set the weights down with a flat back.
exercises.tip: Shoulders down and back, ribs down. Don't let the weights pull you into a slouch.

howto.setup: Pick up heavy dumbbells or handles and stand tall.
howto.mistake: Leaning to one side or shuffling.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
exercises.description: A dip on gymnastic rings, which are unstable, so the chest, triceps and shoulders work harder than on bars and the bottom stretch is deeper.
howTo: Support yourself on the rings with your arms straight and the rings turned slightly out.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows, keeping the rings close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Learn the support hold first. If the rings shake, stick with bar dips for now.

howto.setup: Support yourself on rings with arms straight and rings turned out slightly.
cues: Lower until shoulders are below elbows
Keep the rings close to your body
howto.mistake: Letting the rings drift wide.

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands in low rings, so you can lower below hand level for a deep chest stretch and must stabilise the rings as you press.
howTo: Set the rings a few inches off the floor and get into a push-up position holding them.
Lower your chest between the rings.
Press up and turn the rings out slightly at the top.
exercises.tip: Raise your feet to make it harder.

howto.setup: Set rings a few inches off the floor and get into a push-up position.
cues: Lower your chest to the rings
Press and turn the rings out at the top
howto.mistake: Letting the rings wobble outward.

exercises.name: Ring Row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row on rings, made easier or harder by changing your body angle. The rings let your wrists turn naturally as you pull.
howTo: Hold the rings and lean back with your body straight and your heels on the floor.
Pull your chest up to the rings, turning your palms in as you go.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Walk your feet forward to make it harder.

howto.setup: Hang under rings with body straight and heels on the floor.
cues: Pull your chest between the rings
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag.

exercises.name: Ring Pull-Up
exercises.description: A pull-up on rings, where your grip turns freely from overhand to neutral. Most people find that easier on the elbows and shoulders than a fixed bar.
howTo: Hang from the rings with your arms straight.
Pull your chest up toward the rings, letting your palms turn in.
Lower all the way to a dead hang.
exercises.tip: Keep the rings from swinging. Start each rep from a still hang.

howto.setup: Hang from rings with a neutral grip.
cues: Pull the elbows down to your ribs
howto.mistake: Kipping to finish reps.

exercises.name: Ring Fly
exercises.description: A bodyweight chest fly on rings that loads the chest heavily at long length. You adjust the difficulty with your body angle.
howTo: Hold the rings at chest height and lean forward with your arms straight and slightly bent.
Let your arms open wide as your chest lowers.
Squeeze your arms back together to rise.
exercises.tip: Start very upright. It gets hard quickly as you lean further forward.

howto.setup: Start in a push-up position on rings with arms straight.
howto.mistake: Going wider than you can bring back with control.

exercises.name: Ring Face Pull
exercises.description: A bodyweight face pull on rings for the rear delts and mid traps.
howTo: Hold the rings and lean back with your body straight.
Pull your hands toward your forehead, elbows high and wide.
Lower with control.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows at shoulder height or higher.

howto.setup: Stand facing the rings at a lean with arms straight.
cues: Pull the rings toward your face
howto.mistake: Bending at the hips to cheat.

exercises.name: Ring Biceps Curl
exercises.description: A bodyweight curl on rings: lean back and curl your body up toward your hands.
howTo: Hold the rings with your palms up and lean back with your arms straight.
Curl your hands toward your forehead, keeping your elbows pointed forward.
Lower with control.
exercises.tip: Keep your body straight. Don't let your hips sag to finish the rep.

howto.setup: Lean back holding rings with palms up and arms straight.
cues: Curl your body toward your hands
howto.mistake: Pulling with the back instead of the arms.

exercises.name: Ring Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A bodyweight triceps extension on rings with your arms overhead, which loads the long head in a stretched position.
howTo: Hold the rings at chest height and lean forward with your arms straight.
Bend your elbows so your forehead moves toward the rings.
Push back out to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows pointing forward and your body rigid.

howto.setup: Lean into the rings with arms straight in front of you.
cues: Bend the elbows to bring your head between your hands
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag as you push back.

exercises.name: Ring L-Sit
exercises.description: A support hold on rings with your legs held straight out in front, for the abs and hip flexors. It's a strength skill rather than a size builder.
howTo: Support yourself on the rings with your arms straight.
Lift your legs straight out in front until they're level.
Hold for time, keeping your shoulders pressed down.
exercises.tip: Tuck your knees in if you can't hold straight legs yet.

howto.setup: Support yourself on rings with arms straight and legs extended forward.
howto.mistake: Letting the shoulders shrug up.

exercises.name: Suspension Row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row on suspension straps, where your body angle sets the difficulty.
howTo: Hold the handles and lean back with your body straight.
Pull your chest to the handles, elbows close.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Walk your feet forward to make it harder.

howto.setup: Hold the handles and lean back with your body straight.
cues: Pull your chest to the hands
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag.

exercises.name: Suspension Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your feet or hands in suspension straps, which adds an instability challenge.
howTo: Put your feet in the foot cradles and get into a push-up position.
Lower your chest to the floor.
Press back up, keeping your hips level.
exercises.tip: Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.

howto.setup: Set your feet in the straps or hands in the handles in a push-up position.
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag.

exercises.name: Suspension Y/T Raise
exercises.description: A bodyweight raise into a Y or T shape on suspension straps, for the rear delts and lower and mid traps.
howTo: Hold the handles and lean back with your arms straight in front of you.
Raise your arms out into a Y or a T, pulling your body up.
Lower with control.
exercises.tip: Keep your arms straight. The lean angle sets the load.

howto.setup: Hold the handles and lean back with arms straight in front.
cues: Raise the arms into a Y or T
howto.mistake: Bending the arms to pull.

exercises.name: Suspension Biceps Curl
exercises.description: A bodyweight biceps curl on suspension straps.
howTo: Hold the handles with your palms up and lean back with your arms straight.
Curl your hands toward your forehead, elbows fixed.
Lower with control.
exercises.tip: Point your elbows at the anchor and keep them there.

howto.setup: Lean back holding the handles with palms up.
cues: Curl your hands toward your forehead
howto.mistake: Dropping the elbows during the rep.

exercises.name: Suspension Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A bodyweight overhead triceps extension on suspension straps, which loads the long head when stretched.
howTo: Face away from the anchor holding the handles, and lean forward with your arms straight.
Bend your elbows to bring your head between your hands.
Push back out to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows narrow and your body straight.

howto.setup: Face away from the anchor holding the handles at arm's length.
cues: Bend the elbows to lower your head
howto.mistake: Letting the elbows flare wide.

exercises.name: Suspension Pistol Squat (Assisted)
exercises.description: A one-leg squat holding suspension straps for balance and a little help, building toward a full pistol.
howTo: Hold the handles and stand on one leg with the other straight out in front.
Sit down as low as you can on one leg, pulling on the straps only as needed.
Stand back up.
exercises.tip: Use the straps as little as possible.

howto.setup: Hold the handles and stand on one leg.
cues: Sit down on the working leg
Use the straps only as needed
howto.mistake: Pulling with the arms to stand.

exercises.name: Suspension Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: A lying leg curl with your heels in suspension straps, combined with a hip bridge, for the hamstrings.
howTo: Lie on your back with your heels in the foot cradles and lift your hips.
Pull your heels toward your glutes, keeping your hips up.
Straighten your legs slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips high the whole set.

howto.setup: Lie on your back with heels in the straps and hips lifted.
cues: Curl the heels toward your glutes
howto.mistake: Dropping the hips during the curl.

exercises.name: Suspension Fallout
exercises.description: A standing rollout on suspension straps for the abs, with the load set by how far you lean.
howTo: Hold the handles with straight arms and lean forward on your toes.
Let your arms rise overhead as your body falls forward.
Pull back up using your abs.
exercises.tip: Keep your ribs down. Don't let your lower back sag.

howto.setup: Hold the handles and lean forward with arms straight.
cues: Let the arms rise overhead as you lean
howto.mistake: Letting the lower back sag.

exercises.name: Suspension Pike
exercises.description: A pike from a push-up position with your feet in suspension straps, for the abs.
howTo: Get into a plank with your feet in the foot cradles.
Lift your hips high and pull your feet toward your hands with straight legs.
Lower back to the plank.
exercises.tip: Lead with your hips, not your knees.

howto.setup: Set your feet in the straps in a push-up position.
cues: Lift the hips toward the ceiling
howto.mistake: Bending the knees instead of piking.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description: A two-hand hip-hinge swing for powerful hip extension and conditioning. It's good for the glutes and hamstrings, but more for power than for size.
howTo: Stand with the bell slightly in front, hinge and grip it with both hands.
Hike it back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to float it to chest height.
Let it swing back and hinge into the next rep.
exercises.tip: It's a hinge, not a squat. Drive with your hips, not your arms.

howto.setup: Stand with the bell a foot in front of you and hinge to grip it.
cues: Hike the bell back between your legs
Let the bell float to chest height
howto.mistake: Squatting the swing instead of hinging.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
exercises.description: A front squat with two kettlebells racked at your chest, which keeps you upright and works your core hard.
howTo: Clean two bells to the rack position, elbows tucked.
Squat down between your hips as deep as you can control.
Drive back up.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows in and your chest tall.

howto.setup: Hold one or two bells in the rack position at your chest.
howto.mistake: Letting the bells pull your torso forward.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
exercises.description: A swing that finishes with the bell in the rack position at your shoulder. It's a power and technique lift and builds little muscle.
howTo: Hike the bell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward and pull the bell close to your body.
Let it land softly in the rack with your wrist straight.
exercises.tip: Keep it close so it doesn't flip onto your forearm.

howto.setup: Hinge and grip the bell between your feet.
cues: Drive the hips and pull the elbow close
Rotate the bell softly into the rack
howto.mistake: Letting the bell flip over and bang the forearm.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Press
exercises.description: A strict one-arm overhead press from the rack position. The offset bell makes your shoulder and trunk work to keep it steady.
howTo: Clean the bell to the rack and brace.
Press it straight overhead, letting your forearm stay vertical.
Lower back to the rack.
exercises.tip: Squeeze the glute on the same side to keep from leaning.

howto.setup: Start with the bell in the rack position.
howto.mistake: Leaning back to press.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Push Press
exercises.description: An overhead press driven by a short knee dip, so you can handle more weight than strict.
howTo: Rack the bell, dip your knees slightly.
Drive up with your legs and press the bell overhead in one move.
Lower to the rack under control.
exercises.tip: Dip straight down. Don't lean forward.

howto.setup: Start with the bell in the rack position.
howto.mistake: Dipping too deep and losing the drive.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.description: A one-arm swing that finishes with the bell locked out overhead. It's a power and conditioning lift.
howTo: Hike the bell back between your legs.
Drive your hips and pull the bell up close to your body.
Punch your hand through as it passes your head and lock out overhead.
exercises.tip: Learn the swing and clean first.

howto.setup: Hinge and grip the bell between your feet.
cues: Drive the hips and pull high
howto.mistake: Letting the bell flop over and crash onto the wrist.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.description: A slow move from lying to standing with a bell held overhead, for shoulder stability and trunk control rather than muscle size.
howTo: Lie with the bell pressed up over one shoulder.
Roll to your elbow, then your hand, and lift your hips.
Sweep your leg under you, kneel, then stand, keeping the bell over your shoulder.
Reverse the steps to lie back down.
exercises.tip: Keep your eyes on the bell and move slowly.

howto.setup: Lie on your back holding a bell overhead with one arm locked.
cues: Keep your eyes on the bell
howto.mistake: Rushing the steps and losing a vertical arm.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Single-Leg RDL
exercises.description: A one-leg hinge with a kettlebell, which loads the hamstrings and glutes at long length and challenges your balance.
howTo: Stand on one leg with a bell in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward as your free leg reaches back, until your hamstring stretches.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips square to the floor.

howto.setup: Stand on one leg holding the bell in the opposite hand.
cues: Hinge forward as the free leg rises
Stand by driving the hip forward
howto.mistake: Opening the hips toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Row
exercises.description: A one-arm row with a kettlebell, supported on a bench or in a staggered stance.
howTo: Brace one hand on a bench and hold the bell with your arm straight.
Row it toward your hip.
Lower to a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Pull your elbow back toward your hip, not straight up.

howto.setup: Hinge with one hand braced and the bell hanging below.
cues: Row the bell toward your hip
howto.mistake: Twisting the torso to finish.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description: A side hinge with a bell held overhead, for the obliques and shoulder stability.
howTo: Press a bell overhead and turn your feet away from it.
Push your hip out and hinge sideways, sliding your free hand down your leg.
Return to standing, keeping your arm vertical.
exercises.tip: Keep your eyes on the bell and your arm locked.

howto.setup: Press a bell overhead and turn your feet out to the side.
cues: Hinge sideways down the other leg
howto.mistake: Bending the elbow of the top arm.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.description: A one-hand carry that makes your trunk resist leaning, for the obliques, grip and traps.
howTo: Pick up a heavy bell in one hand.
Walk tall for a set distance without leaning.
Switch hands.
exercises.tip: Stand as if you were carrying nothing.

howto.setup: Hold one heavy bell or dumbbell at your side.
howto.mistake: Leaning toward the weight.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo
exercises.description: A slow circle of a light bell around your head. It's mainly a shoulder warm-up and builds little muscle.
howTo: Hold the bell by the horns upside down at your chest.
Circle it around your head, keeping it close.
Reverse direction each rep.
exercises.tip: Keep your ribs down and stay tall.

howto.setup: Hold the bell upside down by the horns at your chest.
cues: Circle the bell around your head
howto.mistake: Arching the back as the bell passes behind you.

exercises.name: Muscle-Up
exercises.description: A pull-up that transitions over the bar or rings into a dip, an advanced skill for pulling and pushing strength.
howTo: Hang with a false grip if you're using rings.
Pull explosively to your lower chest.
Lean forward over the bar and press out of the dip to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Strict pull-ups to the chest and deep dips come first.

howto.setup: Hang from a bar or rings with a false or overhand grip.
cues: Turn the wrists over the bar
howto.mistake: Chicken-winging one arm over at a time.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
exercises.description: A wide push-up that shifts your weight to one arm while the other stays straight, a step toward a one-arm push-up.
howTo: Set your hands very wide.
Lower toward one hand, keeping the other arm straight.
Press back up and alternate sides.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips level as you shift.

howto.setup: Set your hands very wide in a push-up position.
howto.mistake: Letting the hips twist.

exercises.name: Pseudo-Planche Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands turned out by your hips and your body leaning forward, which shifts the load to the front delts.
howTo: Set your hands by your lower ribs with your fingers turned out, and lean forward.
Lower while keeping the forward lean.
Press back up without losing the lean.
exercises.tip: Lean less if your wrists complain.

howto.setup: Set your hands by your waist with fingers out and lean forward.
howto.mistake: Losing the lean so it becomes a normal push-up.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Push-Up
exercises.description: A vertical push-up in a handstand against a wall, a demanding bodyweight shoulder press.
howTo: Kick up into a handstand with your heels on the wall.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Use a mat under your head and lower slowly.

howto.setup: Kick up into a handstand facing away from the wall.
cues: Lower your head to the floor
howto.mistake: Arching the back to press.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.description: A full one-leg squat with the other leg held out in front, needing strength, balance and mobility.
howTo: Stand on one leg with the other leg out in front.
Sit down as low as you can on one leg.
Stand back up without touching down.
exercises.tip: Hold a light weight out in front to help with balance.

howto.setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight in front.
cues: Sit down on the working leg
howto.mistake: Dropping fast into the bottom.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.description: A one-leg squat holding your back foot behind you. It's very knee-dominant and stretches the quads.
howTo: Stand on one leg, holding your other foot behind you.
Lower until your back knee touches the floor.
Drive back up.
exercises.tip: Touch down on a pad to start.

howto.setup: Stand on one leg holding the other foot behind you.
cues: Lower the back knee to the floor
Drive up through the front foot
howto.mistake: Letting the front heel lift.

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever Row
exercises.description: A row done while holding a tucked front lever under a bar or rings, an advanced bodyweight back exercise.
howTo: Hang from the bar and pull into a tucked front lever with your body horizontal.
Row your chest toward the bar.
Lower back to the lever without dropping your hips.
exercises.tip: Master the tuck hold first.

howto.setup: Hang in a front lever or tuck lever position under the bar.
cues: Row the bar to your waist
howto.mistake: Letting the hips drop below the line.

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever Hold
exercises.description: A straight-arm hold with your body horizontal and knees tucked, working the lats and abs.
howTo: Hang from the bar.
Pull your shoulders down and tuck your knees, lifting your hips until your back is level.
Hold for time.
exercises.tip: Arms stay straight. Pull down with the lats.

howto.setup: Hang from the bar and pull your knees to your chest.
cues: Press the bar down with straight arms
howto.mistake: Bending the arms to hold the position.

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
exercises.description: An advanced ab exercise lowering a rigid body from vertical while holding a bench behind your head.
howTo: Lie on a bench holding it behind your head.
Lift your body to vertical, resting on your upper back.
Lower your straight body slowly toward the bench, then raise it again.
exercises.tip: Start with the lowering only.

howto.setup: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head.
cues: Lift your body onto your upper back
howto.mistake: Bending at the hips.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.description: A gymnastics core hold: lower back pressed into the floor, arms and legs raised. It's good for core control, with a modest muscle stimulus.
howTo: Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your arms, shoulders and legs a few inches.
Hold for time.
exercises.tip: If your back lifts, bend your knees.

howto.setup: Lie on your back with arms overhead.
cues: Press the lower back into the floor
howto.mistake: Letting the lower back lift.

exercises.name: L-Sit (Floor or Parallettes)
exercises.description: A support hold on the floor or parallettes with your legs held out straight, for the abs and hip flexors.
howTo: Put your hands beside your hips and press down.
Lift your hips and legs until your legs are straight out in front.
Hold for time.
exercises.tip: Tuck your knees in if you can't straighten your legs yet.

howto.setup: Sit between parallettes and press up with straight arms.
cues: Lift the legs to hip height
howto.mistake: Bending the knees.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.description: An explosive jump onto a box. It's for power, not size: the muscle stimulus is low, but it trains rate of force.
howTo: Stand a short step from the box.
Swing your arms and jump up, landing softly with bent knees.
Step down, don't jump down.
exercises.tip: A higher box isn't the goal. Land quietly.

howto.setup: Stand a foot in front of a box with feet hip width.
howto.mistake: Picking a box so high you land in a deep squat.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.description: A standing jump forward for distance. It's a power exercise, not a size builder.
howTo: Stand with feet hip width.
Swing your arms back, then jump forward as far as you can.
Land softly in a squat.
exercises.tip: Stick the landing before the next rep.

howto.setup: Stand with feet hip width and swing the arms back.
howto.mistake: Landing with straight legs.

exercises.name: Depth Jump
exercises.description: A step off a low box straight into an immediate jump. It's high-impact power training, not hypertrophy.
howTo: Step off a low box.
As soon as your feet hit the ground, jump up as high as you can.
Land softly.
exercises.tip: Keep ground contact short. Use a low box.

howto.setup: Step off a low box and land with both feet.
howto.mistake: Using a box so high the landing slows the jump.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.description: A squat into a jump for lower-body power. It builds little muscle.
howTo: Squat to about parallel.
Explode up into a jump.
Land softly and sink into the next rep.
exercises.tip: Quality over quantity. Stop when the jumps get lower.

howto.setup: Stand with feet shoulder width.
cues: Land softly into the next rep
howto.mistake: Landing stiff-legged.

exercises.name: Bounding
exercises.description: Exaggerated running strides for distance, for sprint and leg power rather than size.
howTo: Run in long, springy strides, driving your knee up.
Push off hard and stay in the air on each stride.
Land on the ball of your foot and repeat.
exercises.tip: Do these on grass or a track, and stop when your form slips.

howto.setup: Start with a short run-up.
howto.mistake: Taking short steps instead of long bounds.

exercises.name: Plyometric Push-Up
exercises.description: An explosive push-up where your hands leave the floor. It's for upper-body power, not size.
howTo: Get into a push-up position.
Lower, then push up explosively so your hands leave the floor.
Land softly and go into the next rep.
exercises.tip: Land with soft elbows.

howto.setup: Get into a push-up position.
cues: Push explosively so hands leave the floor
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag on landing.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.description: An overhead throw that slams a ball into the ground, for power and conditioning.
howTo: Raise the ball overhead, on your toes.
Slam it down in front of you, hinging and bracing.
Catch it on the bounce or pick it up, then repeat.
exercises.tip: Use a dead-bounce slam ball.

howto.setup: Hold a slam ball overhead with arms extended.
howto.mistake: Using only the arms.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.description: An explosive two-hand pass from the chest against a wall, for upper-body power.
howTo: Hold the ball at your chest facing a wall.
Throw it hard into the wall from your chest.
Catch it and repeat.
exercises.tip: Throw it fast. The throw is the point.

howto.setup: Stand facing a wall holding a med ball at your chest.
howto.mistake: Throwing with the arms only and no leg drive.

exercises.name: Barbell Rollout
exercises.description: A kneeling rollout with a loaded barbell, the same as the ab wheel with a wider, steadier base.
howTo: Kneel behind a barbell with small plates on it, hands on the bar.
Roll it forward, letting your body extend while your ribs stay down.
Pull it back using your abs.
exercises.tip: Only go as far as you can without your lower back sagging.

howto.setup: Kneel with a loaded barbell under your shoulders.
howto.mistake: Letting the lower back sag.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Rollout
exercises.description: An easier rollout with your forearms on a stability ball, a good starting point before the ab wheel.
howTo: Kneel with your forearms on a ball.
Roll it forward, extending your body.
Pull it back with your abs.
exercises.tip: Keep a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.

howto.setup: Kneel with forearms on a stability ball.
howto.mistake: Letting the hips sag.

exercises.name: Standing Ab-Wheel Rollout
exercises.description: An ab-wheel rollout started from standing, a very hard and long lever version of the kneeling rollout.
howTo: Stand with the wheel on the floor in front of you, legs straight.
Roll out until your body is nearly parallel with the floor.
Pull back up with your abs.
exercises.tip: Only for people who own the kneeling version. Roll up a slope to start.

howto.setup: Stand with feet hip width holding an ab wheel.
cues: Roll forward as far as you can control
howto.mistake: Rolling past the point you can return from.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.description: A passive hang from a bar for grip endurance and shoulder decompression. It builds little muscle.
howTo: Grip the bar about shoulder width apart.
Let your body hang with your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
Hold for time.
exercises.tip: Breathe slowly and stay relaxed.

howto.setup: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width grip.
howto.mistake: Bending the arms to hold on.

exercises.name: Active (Scapular) Hang
exercises.description: A hang with your shoulders pulled down and back, which builds shoulder control for pull-ups.
howTo: Hang from the bar.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears without bending your arms.
Hold for time.
exercises.tip: The arms stay straight. Only the shoulder blades move.

howto.setup: Hang from a bar with arms straight.
cues: Pull the shoulders down away from your ears
howto.mistake: Bending the elbows to fake the hold.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
exercises.description: Small reps of pulling your shoulders down from a dead hang, for scapular strength and control.
howTo: Hang from the bar with your arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades down so your body rises an inch or two.
Lower back to the hang.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows locked.

howto.setup: Hang from a bar with arms straight.
howto.mistake: Bending the elbows during the rep.

patterns_note: v5: `patterns` = movement-slot ids from patterns.json (first = main slot). Model choice, not measured.
bodyweight_note: v6: bodyweight_fraction = share of body mass the exercise moves (0-1; omitted = external load only). effective load = fraction x bodyweight + added load (bodyweight_assisted machines: minus assistance). basis: measured (force plate, Ebben 2011 doi:10.1519/JSC.0b013e31820c8587), derived (from segment masses, Plagenhoef 1983 doi:10.1080/02701367.1983.10605290, men), modeling (our estimate). Holds, jumps, rollouts and angle-dependent suspension isolation moves are left without a fraction. A model, not a measurement.
swap_note: v7: swap = attributes for swap difference lines (rules.json swap_tags). Ordinals are 1-3 on the swap_tags scale; flags list the flag tags that apply. Method: defaults by equipment and type (machine/cable/Smith stability 3, free weight 2, rings/suspension 1; loading primary 3, accessory 2, isolation 1; systemic fatigue from type plus the fatigue field; stretch 3 if in rules.json stretch_biased, else 2; isolation 3 for guided single-joint, 2 free single-joint, 1 compound), then hand overrides per exercise. Tags describe tendencies, not guarantees, and make no medical claims. See data/swaptags-spec.md.
equipment_needs_note: v8: equipment_needs = list of required items from rules.json equipment_items; each item is one token or "a|b" (any one of them); all items are needed together; [] = bodyweight only (floor or wall). Hand-reviewed from each exercise's equipment, name and howto (tools/equipment_needs_data.py); `equipment` is unchanged and still drives swap scoring, logging and load steps. Small improvised accessories (handles, ankle cuffs, a step) are not listed.
